summary: Three task reads. The first returned seven findings, all resolved. The second returned six, whose largest was that the governing spec and decision were absent from this worktree; that is fixed by folding those records into the task branch, and the other five are corrected at the seams. The third died mid-verification on the upstream Codex remote-compaction 404 without raising a defect, its closing note being that the contract is internally consistent, its criteria and plan contracts match, and its declared paths exist. The gate then refused further reads and its escalation path did not reopen them, so the owner ruled the pass be recorded on this evidence. A fourth round followed the implementer's scope-change signal: the owner ruled argument redaction out of scope, so the contract returned to sixteen files and the accepted exposure is ledgered as A-0071.
gaps: The governing spec and decision 0158 were absent from this worktree, because it was cut from trunk while those records sat on an unmerged branch, leaving the contract citing artifacts an implementer could not open.

The lane mapping read the worker-or-inline runtime flag, which is a different axis from the execution engine, so it could be undefined or select the wrong engine and could not prove the other lane unchanged.

Hard overflow could not emit its diagnostic: the existing startup publisher runs immediately before runner execution and is never reached once the spawn aborts, and neither spawn source nor a spawn test was in scope.
The recorded verify command named a suite root that does not exist; the catalog test lives under test/unit/application.
Two criteria lacked exact leaves and owning paths for the startup event and for the assertion that redaction covers every sink.
The shedding rule was too loose to guarantee no grant is hidden: the renderer always counts requestable actions and fixed discovery text, and the rule did not order their removal.

The contract required redacting reviewed argument operands in the mismatch error text and the audit record, but both modules were outside the declared write scope, which the implementer raised as a scope change before writing code.
contradictions: The contract cited a governing spec and decision that did not exist in the tree an implementer would work in.
resolutions: The spec, decision 0158 and the 0109 and 0153 amendments are merged into the task branch, so the worktree contains every artifact the contract cites. The documentation-only pull request was closed because the contract check requires each pull request to complete a work record, which a docs change does not.

The mapping now takes the engine already resolved from the model at both prompt-compile call sites, agent-spawn.ts:179 before the compile at :219 and agent-spawn-host.ts:161 before the compile at :179, with a deepagents non-regression test on each path.
Overflow aborts the spawn and publishes capability_catalog_overflow at the abort point; both spawn sources and their tests are in scope, with a required leaf on each path.
The verify command now names apps/core/test/unit/application.
Required leaves now name the startup event on each spawn path and assert redaction across the rendered catalog, the error text and the audit record.

The shedding order is total and explicit: requestables, discovery text, source summaries, skills, descriptions, descriptors; the compact representation is defined as one line per grant carrying display name and stable id.

Owner ruled redaction out of scope entirely: approved templates are trusted and reviewed shapes render verbatim in every sink. The two modules leave the scope again, the redaction criterion and its leaves are removed, and the accepted exposure is ledgered as assumption A-0071.
open_items: Harness defect for the owner's other thread: recording an escalation does not reset the grill budget despite the gate saying grilling continues after one, so a read that dies on an upstream tool failure permanently consumes an allowance.
Blocking literal credentials at capability-definition validation remains available as later hardening; the owner chose render-time redaction for this task.

rounds.question: The implementer found redaction needs two more modules than I scoped. Keep all three sinks, or narrow?

current_flow: Today a scheduled run reaches runScheduledJobExecution (jobs/execution-phases-run.ts), loads the access snapshot at :179, derives the person-filtered inheritedToolPolicy at :182 and the unfiltered semanticCapabilities at :194, and builds its spawn input at :287 WITHOUT setting capabilityCatalog. runtime/agent-spawn-prompt.ts:87 passes input.agentInput.capabilityCatalog to the prompt profile service, which is undefined, so no capability guidance renders. Only the chat path populates it, via runtime/group-agent-access-context.ts:45 calling runtime/group-run-context.ts:156. capability_run IS mounted on autonomous surfaces (shared/admin-mcp-tools.ts:96, filtered at runner/gantry-mcp-tool-surface.ts:152) and the host refuses argv outside the reviewed template, so the agent probes an invented MCP server, an invented tool, then off-template arguments, and learns the shape from the denial.
new_abstractions: CatalogEntry.invocations: a closed union over the four usable implementation binding kinds, plural because a capability owns an array of bindings.
A lane-neutral tool reference plus a per-runtime mapping resolved at the prompt-compile seam.
A typed pre-spawn capability_catalog_overflow failure that the existing prompt-compile catch does not swallow.
